poems:
10:00. The kitchen goes off duty.
The counter holds one glass nobody claims.

The relief nurse signs in at 10:01,
still holding her car keys.

A porch bulb, a moth,
a screen door that doesn't quite latch.

You both sit on the bed with your shoes still on.
This is the conversation.

Checked:
stove
back door
kid's forehead
phone charger
back door again
Somewhere a parking garage gate comes down.

The last email of the day goes out at 10:06,
cc'ing three people who will not read it for two days.

Upstairs, a bedroom door closes with the particular softness
of someone who is not going to sleep.

Nightcap, n.
A drink you have because the day would otherwise just end.
A city bus with four riders, all of them sitting apart.

In every watch advertisement ever printed, it is 10:10.
Somewhere a photographer is still setting the hands.
The ice maker dumps a tray and startles only the dog.

Turn the porch bulb off.
Leave the one over the stove.
That is the whole system.
A trash can wheeled to the curb, one wheel complaining.

Somebody's mother is being helped into bed by somebody's daughter,
and neither of them is talking about it.

"Just leave it, I'll do it in the morning."
Nobody does it in the morning.

The last kitchen in the strip mall goes down to one cook
scraping a flat top.

10:17 and the baby is finally down,
which means you have forty minutes
and no idea what to do with them.

Three floors of an office building still on,
all of it for one guy and a vacuum.
A cat arrives on the bed like a decision that has already been made.

10:20. Chairs upside down on tables.
The mop bucket arrives on three good wheels.
Deadbolt, chain, then the deadbolt again.

10:22, and the house makes the noise it makes
when it thinks no one is listening.

The dryer buzzer goes off.
It will go off again in an hour, and again.
Somewhere a shift starts with a clipboard.
A teenager negotiating with a phone she has been told twice to put down.

Gas station at 10:26.
One car, two attendants, and a hot dog
that has outlived everyone's expectations.

Your father went down at nine and will report tomorrow
that he barely closed his eyes.
Blue glow on a ceiling, moving.

The security guard's radio says nothing all night
and he keeps it on anyway.
10:30, and the last bus of any use pulls out.

10:31. Flossing, briefly and angrily,
to the memory of the dentist's voice.

Two hospital elevators, one of them going down
with someone who came in walking.

Tomorrow:
call the dentist
transfer the money
be different
The neighbor's motion sensor catches a possum and announces it to no one.

The bookmark has not moved in three nights.
The book forgives this.

10:36. The thermostat clicked down an hour ago.
The blanket economy begins.
Somewhere a plane is being cleaned by people who will never fly on it.
A bike chained to a rail overnight.
Bar filling, or emptying, depending on the bar.

At 10:40 the second wind arrives, uninvited,
and stays until it has ruined tomorrow.

The dog does the three-circle thing on the rug.
Nobody has ever explained it.

Kitchen towel over the oven handle,
folded by someone who cared for eleven seconds.
An engine ticking as it cools.

The night baker's alarm is set for 1:15
and he is still up, which is his own business.

Set out the mug.
Fill the reservoir.
Press nothing.
The machine handles the rest at six.

A woman on a treadmill in an apartment gym, alone, at 10:46,
running toward nothing in particular.

Every child in the house is asleep
and both parents are pretending not to notice they could talk.

Ten minutes, n.
The amount of time either of us will admit to having left.

A key turns two doors down.
Everyone hears it. Nobody cares.
Streetlamp, asphalt, a shopping cart nobody will claim.

10:51. The math starts.
If I fall asleep right now.

The night nurse learns which patient will pull the sensor off,
and how many times.
A garage door closing on a lawnmower, a canoe, and no car.

At 10:54 the text gets typed, read back, and deleted.
Correctly.
Down the hall, a fan set to the speed that means someone is serious.
A glass of melted ice on a coaster.

10:57. One more episode autoplays
into a room that had decided against it.
At 10:58 the dog is walked by whoever lost.

One bulb left on in the kitchen, on purpose,
for whoever comes in later.
